text: Reinforcement Learning: · TD-Gammon p. 445 · 81% ∨ Tinct text

The 198 figure comes from how finely each point's occupancy is encoded, not from the number of points alone. For each of the 24 points, Tesauro used four units per color to capture distinctions that matter strategically: whether there's a single exposed piece (a "blot"), two or more pieces (a "made point," safe from being hit), exactly three pieces ("single spare"), and a scaled value for more than three ("multiple spares"). That's 4 units × 2 colors × 24 points = 192 units.

The remaining 6 units cover pieces on the bar (one each for white and black), pieces already borne off (one each), and two units marking whose turn it is.

So the richness isn't in the number of locations but in giving the network a feature-rich, pre-scaled description of each location's state—something the text notes required "substantial knowledge of how ANNs work and how information is best presented to them," even though it avoided hand-crafted backgammon strategy knowledge.
